Want your child to listen the first time? 👟 Say it once, then stop talking.

Daisy is five. "Shoes on." She's loading… "Shoes ON." "Daisy, SHOES!" Ten times. 😩 But every time you say it again, her little brain starts over.

What's happening in her head: ears 👂 → brain 🧠 → feet 👣. Research shows young children can take around twice as long as adults to process the same words. She's not ignoring you. She's still loading. ⏳

Put yourself in her shoes: what if every time you started to move, someone restarted your instructions? So try this:
1️⃣ Say it once, then stop talking. 🤫 Count quietly in your head.
2️⃣ Move your feet, not your mouth. Walk over instead of saying it again.

Try it for one whole week. By Wednesday it's faster. By Friday, she's at the door before you are. 🚪 And at bedtime, Daisy whispers, "Mom… you don't yell anymore." ❤️

"Be still, and know that I am God." Psalm 46:10 (ESV) 🙏 God doesn't need to shout over us. When Jesus spoke from the cross, it was finished, and He rose again.

And if your child's mind is still loading "what if…?" late at night, that may be worry. ❤️
